Name: Ortiz Bonito del Norte Tuna in Olive Oil
Description: Bonito del Norte is the finest tuna in the North Atlantic. Ortiz has been hand-packing it from the Bay of Biscay since 1891, using pole-and-line methods that target individual fish rather than whole schools. Packed in olive oil, the flesh stays firm and distinctly flavoured — not the flaked, salted filler of mass production. A benchmark for what canned tuna can be.
PillarGood: Bonito del Norte (Thunnus alalunga) is a distinct species from the more common skipjack or yellowfin sold simply as 'tuna'. Ortiz declares the species, the catch area, and the oil used. Flesh is white, firm, and genuinely flavourful without added flavour enhancers.
PillarClean: Pole-and-line caught from the Bay of Biscay. The catch method is declared on-pack. No net fishing. Origin is specific and verifiable. Packed in olive oil, not a vegetable oil blend.
PillarFair: Family-owned company based in Ondarroa, Basque Country, with direct relationships with local fishing fleets that have operated in the same waters for generations.
PillarTrue: Bonito del Norte has centuries of history in Basque fishing culture. Ortiz preserves the traditional preparation — hand-cleaned, lightly cooked, packed whole in olive oil — without industrial shortcuts.

Name: Ortiz Cantabrian Anchovy Fillets in Olive Oil
Description: The Cantabrian anchovy (bocarte) is the gold standard of preserved anchovies. Ortiz catches the fish in spring, when they are fattest, then cures them in salt for 6 to 12 months before cleaning and packing in olive oil. The result is a deeply savoury, silky fillet — far removed from the harsh, overly salty anchovies found in most supermarkets. Used by cooks across Europe and beyond to add depth to almost any dish.
PillarGood: Ingredients: anchovies, olive oil, salt. Nothing else. The curing process is natural — no artificial preservatives, no additives. What is declared on the label is what is in the tin.
PillarClean: Caught in the Cantabrian Sea during the spring bocarte season. Origin and catch period are documented. The salt-curing and maturing process is traditional and transparent.
PillarFair: Processed in Ondarroa, Basque Country. The anchovy industry is central to the local economy and has maintained traditional craft employment for generations.
PillarTrue: Cantabrian anchovy preservation is a protected regional practice rooted in northern Spanish coastal culture. Ortiz does not source from cheaper Mediterranean or Moroccan fisheries and label them as Cantabrian.

Name: Wild Planet Wild Albacore Tuna
Description: Wild Planet sources albacore tuna from small-boat, troll-caught fisheries in the North Pacific. The fish are younger and smaller than those caught by industrial longline — which means lower mercury and a shorter supply chain. Packed without added water or broth: just tuna and sea salt. What the label says is what is in the can.
PillarGood: Ingredients: albacore tuna, sea salt. No water, no vegetable broth, no fillers. Naturally higher in omega-3 than skipjack. The single-cook-in-can method retains nutrients that drain away when fish are pre-cooked and then packed in added liquid.
PillarClean: Troll and pole-and-line caught. Bycatch is negligible with these methods. Wild Planet publishes its sourcing fisheries by species. No FAD (fish aggregating device) fishing.
PillarFair: California-based company with third-party audited supply chain standards. Small-boat fishing fleets are supported rather than displaced by industrial operations.
PillarTrue: Species is declared as albacore — not sold generically as 'white tuna' or 'premium tuna', labelling practices that obscure species identity and make meaningful comparison impossible.

Name: Wild Planet Wild Sardines in Extra Virgin Olive Oil
Description: Pacific sardines are a fast-reproducing, short-lived fish — one of the most sustainable protein sources available anywhere. Wild Planet packs them in extra virgin olive oil with minimal processing, leaving the fish as whole as possible. Rich in omega-3 fatty acids, calcium, and vitamin D. A practical, nutritious everyday food with a clean ingredient list.
PillarGood: Ingredients: sardines, extra virgin olive oil, sea salt. Naturally high in omega-3, calcium, and vitamin D. No flavour enhancers or fillers.
PillarClean: Caught by purse-seine from well-managed Pacific fisheries. Wild Planet publishes catch area and method. Non-GMO Project verified.
PillarFair: Wild Planet works with fishing fleets operating within regulated catch limits. The California base and transparent sourcing keep the supply chain shorter and more auditable than most canned fish brands.
PillarTrue: Sardines are labelled by species and origin — not relabelled as a premium species or obscured by brand language.

Name: Wild Planet Wild Pacific Mackerel
Description: Pacific mackerel is among the most nutritionally dense and sustainably harvested fish available. Wild Planet sources from Pacific fisheries using methods that minimise bycatch. Like all Wild Planet products, the mackerel is cooked once, in the can — not pre-cooked, drained, and then reliquified with added water or broth.
PillarGood: Ingredients: mackerel, sea salt. Two ingredients. Very high in omega-3 fatty acids — more DHA and EPA per serving than most commonly consumed fish.
PillarClean: Wild-caught from Pacific fisheries. Species and catch method declared. No FAD fishing. Wild Planet publishes sourcing details by product.
PillarFair: Same supply chain standards as Wild Planet's tuna line. Small-boat fisheries supported over industrial fleet operations.
PillarTrue: Pacific mackerel (Scomber japonicus) is declared by species — not relabelled or sold under vague umbrella terms.

Name: Patagonia Provisions Wild Pink Salmon
Description: This pink salmon is caught by reef net off Lummi Island — one of the oldest and most selective fishing methods, practiced for centuries by indigenous communities in the Pacific Northwest. Reef nets catch salmon gently and individually, releasing non-target species unharmed. Patagonia Provisions supports the continuation of this practice. A product with a fully traceable story from water to tin.
PillarGood: Ingredients: pink salmon, sea salt. Cooked once, in the can. Naturally high in omega-3 fatty acids and protein.
PillarClean: Reef-net fishing is among the most selective methods available — minimal bycatch, no seabed damage. Catch origin is specific: Lummi Island, Washington — not a broad 'Pacific' claim.
PillarFair: Patagonia Provisions works directly with the Lummi Nation reef net fishery, supporting indigenous fishing rights and economic sovereignty. The supply chain is short and openly acknowledged.
PillarTrue: Pink salmon is a declared species with a documented catch run. The product does not use vague language like 'wild salmon' without clarifying species and origin. The cultural context of reef net fishing is explained on the label and on the brand website.

Name: Patagonia Provisions Mackerel
Description: Jack mackerel from the highly productive Humboldt Current fishery off Chile. Patagonia Provisions works with fisheries operating under science-based catch limits, using purse-seine methods designed to reduce bycatch. Mackerel is a fast-growing, short-lived species that recovers quickly from fishing pressure — one of the most rational seafood choices available.
PillarGood: Ingredients: mackerel, extra virgin olive oil, sea salt, black pepper. Clean label. Rich in omega-3 and vitamin B12.
PillarClean: Purse-seine caught from the Humboldt Current. Catch method and fishery are named and auditable. Patagonia Provisions publishes its sourcing criteria and supplier relationships.
PillarFair: Patagonia as a company has a strong public record on supply chain standards. Workers in Chilean processing facilities are covered under Chilean labour law with additional third-party audit requirements.
PillarTrue: Species is declared (jack mackerel, Trachurus murphyi). Catch origin is specific. Environmental claims on the label are backed by published evidence — not generic sustainability language.

Name: Patagonia Provisions Anchovies
Description: White anchovies (boquerones) from the Bay of Biscay, marinated in white wine vinegar and packed in olive oil. A different product from the salt-cured red anchovy: milder, firmer, and more accessible to those unfamiliar with preserved fish. Patagonia Provisions sources from the same northern Spanish waters that produce some of the world's finest anchovies.
PillarGood: Ingredients: anchovies, sunflower oil, white wine vinegar, salt. The vinegar marinade is a traditional preservation method. No artificial preservatives.
PillarClean: Bay of Biscay catch, declared on the label. Patagonia Provisions requires suppliers to disclose catch method and fishery management standards.
PillarFair: Processed in northern Spain. Patagonia's supplier standards apply throughout the chain.
PillarTrue: White anchovies (boquerones) are correctly named and distinguished from the more familiar salt-cured variety — they are different products with different flavour profiles and preparation methods. The label does not conflate them.

Name: Fishwife Smoked Atlantic Salmon
Description: Fishwife is a US brand bringing the European tinned fish tradition to a wider audience. Their smoked Atlantic salmon is sourced from ASC-certified farms in Scotland and Norway, cold-smoked before packing. The brand is transparent about its sourcing and has built its identity around ingredient honesty — making quality tinned fish an everyday pantry item rather than a specialty purchase.
PillarGood: Ingredients: Atlantic salmon, sea salt, smoke. Short, clean ingredient list. The smoking process is genuine — not liquid smoke flavouring applied to unsmoked fish.
PillarClean: ASC (Aquaculture Stewardship Council) certified farms. Fishwife discloses the certification body and specific sourcing countries on its website.
PillarFair: Female-founded, US company. Third-party certification (ASC) provides external verification of aquaculture standards.
PillarTrue: Atlantic salmon from named regions (Scotland, Norway). Not labelled as 'wild salmon' — an important distinction since the product is farmed. Fishwife is transparent about this.

Name: Bela Sardines in Extra Virgin Olive Oil
Description: Bela-Olhão has been canning sardines on the southern Portuguese coast since 1925. Their sardines are wild-caught in the Atlantic during the summer season, when the fish are at their fattest and most flavourful. Hand-packed and cooked just once, in the can. The result is a firm, intact fillet in genuinely good olive oil — not broken up in brine or vegetable oil. A straightforward, honest product from a century-old tradition.
PillarGood: Ingredients: sardines, extra virgin olive oil, sea salt. Three ingredients. Cooked once, in the can — retaining the natural oils and nutrients better than products that are pre-cooked and then packed in brine.
PillarClean: Wild-caught in the Atlantic. Portuguese sardines (Sardina pilchardus) are a well-managed species in a regulated fishery. Bela-Olhão declares species and catch area.
PillarFair: A century-old producer in Olhão — a Portuguese town whose economy has been built on fishing and canning for generations. Processing is local to the point of catch.
PillarTrue: Portuguese sardines have a protected geographic identity in the EU. Bela-Olhão does not substitute cheaper sardine species or misrepresent origin. The same production location and method since 1925.

Name: Bela Lightly Smoked Sardines in Lemon Olive Oil
Description: The same wild-caught Atlantic sardines from Bela-Olhão, lightly wood-smoked and packed in olive oil with natural lemon flavour. The smoking is real — applied to the fish before packing, not simulated with liquid smoke additives. A good entry point for those new to tinned fish: the lemon and gentle smoke soften the intensity of the sardine without masking it.
PillarGood: Ingredients: sardines, extra virgin olive oil, natural lemon flavour, salt. Lemon flavour from natural sources. Smoking is real wood smoke, not a liquid flavouring substitute.
PillarClean: Same Atlantic fishery and declaration standards as the original Bela sardines line. Processed in Olhão, Portugal.
PillarFair: Same producer and labour standards as Bela's core line.
PillarTrue: No artificial flavouring or smoke substitutes. Positioned clearly as a flavoured variant of the original sardine — not a different or premium species.
